seo.title: WorkStudio
seo.seo_title: WorkStudio: AI agents platform, no code
seo.seo_description: Design AI agents in plain language, no code: a Copilot builds your workflows, your documents answer, a person approves. Opens from your account, in credits.

blocks.role: Promesse de WorkStudio : la pointe de l'IA, extrêmement puissante et extrêmement simple, avec validation humaine.

translation.headline: Leading-edge AI. In plain language. No code.
translation.subheadline: Agents (software that completes a task using the tools you authorize), a Copilot that builds your automations from a plain-language sentence, answers grounded in your own documents: all in one tool, without writing a line of code. A person approves before anything goes out.

blocks.role: Film de WorkStudio : captures réelles de deux exécutions du flux « Tri du courrier entrant » (exemple fictif, boîte de test).

translation.title: WorkStudio at work, from email to send.
translation.body: Two complete runs of the “Incoming mail triage” workflow, captured in WorkStudio: the model sorts the email and writes a draft, the workflow pauses, a person gives approval, then the message is sent. The content is a fictitious example and the message goes to a test mailbox: nothing leaves the network. The slow motion stretches frames that were actually captured, since a run takes about three seconds.
translation.media_alt: Film: WorkStudio sorts an email, prepares a draft, waits for a person's approval, then sends the message to a test mailbox.

blocks.role: Six gestes concrets de WorkStudio, en clair. La preuve est la liste (CL-P03).

translation.title: Leading-edge AI, in plain terms.
translation.intro: One tool, in plain language, for the most recent things AI can do. Here are six concrete steps.

cards.title: Describe it. The Copilot builds it.
cards.text: Write what you want to automate, as you would to a colleague. The Copilot, the creation assistant, prepares a workflow (an automated sequence of tasks); you review it before creating it.

cards.title: Agents that act.
cards.text: An agent is a specialized assistant: it follows your instructions, uses the tools and documents you authorize, and cites its sources.

cards.title: Your documents answer.
cards.text: Ask a question: the answer comes from your own documents, with the source alongside.

cards.title: Paper gets read.
cards.text: Scanned PDFs, images, invoices, quotes: the useful fields are extracted, and anything uncertain is flagged “to verify”.

cards.title: Voice becomes text.
cards.text: Your recordings are transcribed, with a meeting's speakers; a text can also be read aloud.

cards.title: The right model, proof in hand.
cards.text: Compare several models side by side, with the time and tokens (the unit of text a model processes) of each answer, then measure with test sets.

blocks.role: Maquette du flux de facture fournisseur (exemple construit) : du courriel à l'écriture, avec approbation.

translation.title: Describe it. It gets built.
translation.body:
A constructed example, not a result measured at a customer: you write “When a supplier invoice arrives by email, read it, check the maths and prepare the accounting entry.” The Copilot prepares the workflow; you review it, test it step by step, then deploy it.

The workflow stops before writing: a person approves. See this workflow in a demonstration, on fictional data.

items.title: An email arrives.
items.text: The workflow starts when an email reaches a connected service.

items.title: The maths gets checked.
items.text: The invoice is read, its fields extracted and its calculations checked; the workflow concludes “to pay” or “to verify”.

items.title: A person approves.
items.text: The accounting entry is only made after a person approves. The connection to the accounting software is qualified with you.

blocks.role: Scénario type : de la demande à la trace, six temps.

translation.title: From request to trace.
translation.intro: A request's journey, in six stages. Each stage is set up in WorkStudio, without writing code.

cards.title: 1. A request arrives.
cards.text: By email, by a form, by chat, on a schedule or through an automatic call from another piece of software.

cards.title: 2. Information is retrieved.
cards.text: The agent searches the document bases you authorized.

cards.title: 3. A proposal is prepared.
cards.text: A reply draft, a record, a pre-entry line, depending on the case.

cards.title: 4. An approval is requested.
cards.text: The workflow stops on a card showing the planned action. A person approves or refuses.

cards.title: 5. The action runs.
cards.text: Once, if it was authorized. Otherwise, nothing goes out.

cards.title: 6. Everything is traced.
cards.text: Who asked what, what was answered, with which model, in how much time.

blocks.role: Concevoir : agents, flux, Copilote, connaissances, documents et voix. Statuts « disponible » définis (CL-110).

translation.title: Build without writing code.
translation.intro: “Available” means delivered in the current version and verified on Nexora AI's test server. It does not mean a customer is already using it.

cards.title: Agents.
cards.text: A specialized assistant: it follows your instructions, uses the tools and documents you authorize, cites its sources and is published in a chat.

cards.title: Workflows.
cards.text: A sequence of steps, shown as cards or on a canvas (a drawing screen), tested step by step, then deployed through chat, schedule, event or an automatic call from another service. Every deployment is a version you can return to.

cards.title: A Copilot.
cards.text: Describe an automation in plain language: it prepares a workflow you review before creating it. Starter templates for small businesses (quotes, reminders, email sorting, meeting minutes) are provided.

cards.title: Knowledge.
cards.text: A base of your documents, indexed by default on the instance's server: agents answer from it with their sources.

cards.title: Documents read.
cards.text: Reading of scanned PDFs and images, extraction of fields from an invoice, quote, purchase order or expense report, with a “to verify” flag.

cards.title: Voice.
cards.text: Transcription of audio recordings, with a meeting's speakers, and reading a text aloud. No call-answering service is included.

blocks.role: Contrôler : validation, garde-fous, gouvernance, lieu des modèles, engagements sur les données.

translation.title: You keep the controls.
translation.intro: The more powerful a tool is, the more it should stay under your control. Here is how.

cards.title: Human approval.
cards.text: Each action tool of an agent asks, by default, for a person's agreement before writing or deleting. With no answer, the action does not happen.

cards.title: Safeguards.
cards.text: Before going on, you can check that a format is valid, that personal information is absent or masked, or that an answer stays faithful to your knowledge. A safeguard reduces error; it does not eliminate it.

cards.title: Data policies.
cards.text: For each workspace: allow, mask or refuse sending personal information to a model outside the instance. Access groups can forbid certain models.

cards.title: Organizations and roles.
cards.text: Organizations, roles, an audit log and monthly consumption caps. Single sign-on with the usual identity providers.

cards.title: Each model's location.
cards.text: Every model shows whether it runs on your server, in Europe or at a third party. It is a documented display, not proof of residency.

cards.title: Your data stays yours.
cards.text: On your own server, or with us in Quebec: your data never trains a model and is never sold. An external model is only called if you turned it on, in writing, for a specific agent or project.

blocks.role: Mesurer et améliorer : Playground, consignes, traces, évaluations, lots, consommation.

translation.title: Measure, compare, improve.
translation.intro: Choose a model on evidence, not on promises.

cards.title: A Playground.
cards.text: Try and compare several models side by side before choosing, with the time and tokens (the unit of text a model processes) of each answer.

cards.title: Versioned instructions.
cards.text: A reusable instruction has versions and two labels, production and test. You test a version before promoting it; every change is logged.

cards.title: Traces.
cards.text: Every model call leaves a trace: steps, duration, tokens, model. Personal information can be masked in them.

cards.title: Evaluations.
cards.text: Test sets and judges measure whether an agent, an instruction or a model answers well, and compare two versions before changing.

cards.title: Batch processing.
cards.text: Have a table of several hundred rows processed in the background: progress, cancellation, CSV export.

cards.title: Measured consumption.
cards.text: Tokens, runs and estimated carbon footprint, by model, workspace and person, with monthly caps.

blocks.role: Brancher : Nexora Connect, API, site, Assistant, délégation, installation.

cards.title: Connectors.
cards.text: Nexora Connect plugs in a broad catalogue of services: mail, calendar, customer relations, storage, billing. Each connection belongs to a workspace and is qualified service by service.

cards.title: An OpenAI-format API.
cards.text: An API (the door through which other software calls a service) gives access to models and published agents, in the OpenAI format that many tools already understand: keys, quotas, consumption metering.

cards.title: Your website.
cards.text: A published agent shows up on your site with one line of code (chat bubble, frame or link). WorkStudio also installs as an application from a compatible browser.

cards.title: An internal Assistant.
cards.text: A chat where your teams talk to the company's published agents, with their history and attached files.

cards.title: Agents that help each other.
cards.text: An agent can hand a request to another published agent, with limited depth and no loops.

cards.title: A simple installation.
cards.text: One command on a Docker server (a tool that packages software), on Linux or macOS, then backup, restore and update commands.

blocks.role: Comment WorkStudio s'ouvre et ce qu'il consomme : un compte, des crédits (modèles), de l'espace ; la vente n'est pas ouverte.

translation.title: Opens from your account.
translation.body: WorkStudio opens from the “My tools” panel of your Nexora AI account, as long as you have at least one credit left. A plan gives you credits every month and storage space; without a plan, you top up credits. Prices are not published yet: they will appear on the Pricing page once they are published.

items.title: Models use credits.
items.text: Every model an agent or a workflow calls uses credits: one credit equals one Canadian cent of tokens, at the catalogue price. The tokens of each run appear in its traces, and monthly caps limit spending.

items.title: Storage is counted for the organization.
items.text: The storage space of your plan is shared between your products. When it is full, writing is refused with a clear message; reading and deleting stay allowed.

items.title: No credits, nothing erased.
items.text: Calls to models stop with a message that points to top-ups and plans. Your agents, workflows and documents stay where they are; you top up, and everything resumes.

items.title: Not on sale yet.
items.text: Accounts and payments only work in test mode. In the meantime, a demonstration on fictitious data shows the tool.

blocks.role: Hosted agents: agents published in Nexora AI's catalogue are called through the API. The /agents page is no longer in the menus, WorkStudio links to it.

translation.title: Hosted agents, callable by API.
translation.body: An agent built in WorkStudio and published in Nexora AI's catalogue can also be called through the API, the way you call a model. Hosted agents are part of WorkStudio: see the hosted agents catalogue.

items.title: One key, one balance.
items.text: The agent is called with your Nexora AI API key and credit balance, at the real cost of each run.

items.title: Hosting is shown.
items.text: Each agent's page says where its instance runs, what its limits are and how to call it.

items.title: Not on sale yet.
items.text: Sales are not open: accounts and payments only work in test mode, and no price is published.

translation.title: The limits, stated plainly.
translation.body:
A product is also judged by what it writes about its limits. Here are ours, as of this page's date.

On your premises or with us, in Quebec, we start by understanding your case: book an assessment.

The starter models for small businesses are described one by one in the workflow templates. To call a model or an agent with the OpenAI format, see the guide OpenAI-compatible API.

Nexora AI's other tools (code agent, RAG, WebPilot) are gathered in Nexora Apps, with their real state.

items.title: Verified here, not yet at a customer.
items.text: WorkStudio has been verified on Nexora AI's test server with several models hosted elsewhere than on that server. No customer result is announced.

items.title: Tool-using agents need a capable model.
items.text: A small local model is not always enough for agents that call tools. The model is chosen with the case.

items.title: Two options are off the beaten path.
items.text: The code interpreter is off by default and can only be turned on by an administrator. Web search sends its queries outside the instance: it is available only if an administrator turns it on.

items.title: Starter templates are adapted to Quebec, to be validated.
items.text: They are written for Quebec (Canadian dollars, GST and QST), but do not guarantee any tax or legal compliance: your accountant or adviser validates the result.

items.title: Connections are qualified.
items.text: Some services require an administrator to first register an application with the provider, and a public HTTPS address for the instance.

items.question: Can I see it at work before committing?
items.answer: Yes: we offer a demonstration, on fictional data, then we talk about your case. Self-service is not open for sale yet: accounts and payments only work in test mode.

items.question: How much does WorkStudio cost?
items.answer: There is no public price yet. Two things are paid for. Support (assessment, installation, configuration): a written estimate follows the assessment. Use of the platform: in credits, because the models your agents call use them; a plan gives you credits and storage every month, otherwise you top up. Prices will appear on the Pricing page once they are published.

items.question: What uses credits in WorkStudio?
items.answer: Calls to AI models: an agent's answer, reading a document, transcribing a recording. One credit equals one Canadian cent of tokens, at the model catalogue price, and the tokens of each run appear in its traces. When no credits are left, calls are refused and nothing is deleted: you top up, and everything resumes.

items.question: Do I need to know how to code?
items.answer: Not for everyday use: you describe the need in plain language, the Copilot prepares a workflow you review, and the whole thing reads as cards, is set up through forms and is tested step by step. Special cases may need code; we handle that with you.

items.question: Does my data leave my server?
items.answer: By default, indexing of your documents (filing them so they can be found fast) is computed on the instance's server. An external model is never configured without your explicit, written activation, and each model shows where it runs.

items.question: Is my data used to train an AI?
items.answer: No, never. Nexora AI uses neither your data, nor your documents, nor your prompts, nor your results to train or fine-tune a model, and does not sell them.

items.question: Can it integrate with our tools?
items.answer: Yes, through connectors, an OpenAI-format API, or by displaying an agent on your website. Each connection is qualified.

items.question: How long to install?
items.answer: Installation is one command on a Docker server; putting a case into service depends on your situation, with no universal timeline.

translation.title: See WorkStudio at work.
translation.text: We prepare a demonstration on fictitious data, then we talk about your first case. You leave knowing what the tool does, what it does not do, and how credits are counted.
